ambiguous: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware interrupt_on is a declarative fragment inside owner-authored code: it reads like a rules surface but has no command matcher, no precedence over overlapping rules, and no no-match default — it gates by tool name (and optionally an arbitrary-code when predicate) at the Approval layer, not the Decision layer
middleware composition order (before first-to-last, after reverse, wrap nested; DOC) is precedence over code hooks, not over policy rules — do not map it to FP-014-style decision precedence
checkpointer state is both the Approval record (A4 analog: StateSnapshot tasks[].interrupts) and ordinary conversation memory — the same artifact serves two layers and must be attributed per use
layer_vocabulary.notes: rules (the Decision layer): NOT covered — no declarative policy surface, rule language, matcher, or decision checker exists in the documented OSS surface; Decision route is 'no paper surface' and no Decision verdicts are issued. approval (the Approval layer): interrupt() primitive (dynamic, any node or tool; static breakpoints at compile) + LangChain HumanInTheLoopMiddleware (after_model gate, pre-execution; interrupt_on by tool name; decisions approve/edit/reject/respond; batched default or per_call mode; when predicate = arbitrary owner code). sandbox: NOT covered — no sandbox or confinement construct is documented for the OSS library; tool execution is in-process with host privileges, so any confinement is owner-built (tool bodies, wrap_tool_call hooks, external OS/container sandbox). effect (the Effect layer): observed only via the evaluator's instrument (tools/effect_instrument.py sentinel-asset + sandbox-diff model, adapted for in-process execution) against a pinned reference agent — the framework itself emits no effect record beyond ToolMessages in graph state.

policy_ingestion.defaults: No rule match concept exists. With no interrupt() call sites and no HumanInTheLoopMiddleware configured, nothing is gated: every tool call the model proposes executes (DOC: HITL is opt-in middleware; interrupts are explicit call sites). Absence of a gate serializes as unknown with layer attribution in our reporting, never as a framework 'allow' verdict (INV-005 discipline applies to our reporter, not to a framework decision).
policy_ingestion.surface: none — no declarative policy surface; Decision lives in user code. Code-level substitutes the evaluator audits on a pinned reference agent (never ingests as policy): (1) HumanInTheLoopMiddleware interrupt_on dict (tool name -> True | False | InterruptOnConfig{allowed_decisions, description, when}) in create_agent's middleware list; (2) middleware list order and custom AgentMiddleware hooks (before_agent/before_model/after_model/after_agent/wrap_model_call/wrap_tool_call); (3) graph topology (StateGraph nodes/edges/conditional edges, ToolNode reachability); (4) tool registry (tools=[...] of @tool callables); (5) raw interrupt() call sites and compile-time interrupt_before/interrupt_after breakpoints.

spike_answers.a_native_oracle: NO. LangGraph ships no declarative policy surface at all — no policy file format, no allow/ask/deny rule language, no permission config — and therefore no check/evaluate/dry-run entrypoint that could return the framework's own decision for a command under a policy. The documented surface is graphs/nodes/edges/state/checkpointers/stores/interrupts/streaming only (DOC). What decides at runtime is the model (stochastic tool choice) plus owner-authored program code; neither is an oracle.
spike_answers.b_documented_semantics: NO for the Decision layer: a reconstructed route needs a documented rule format, matcher, precedence, and no-match default to reimplement; none exist, so any Decision reconstruction would invent the policy language and the verdict. YES for a narrower Approval-configured analog only: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware interrupt_on semantics are documented exactly at tool-name granularity (True/False/InterruptOnConfig allowed_decisions; batched vs per_call; pre-execution after_model timing), so a static audit of a pinned reference agent's config yields a deterministic configured expectation — labelled evaluation of a configuration, never a Decision verdict. The when predicate is arbitrary owner Python and falls outside the YES.
spike_answers.c_surface_record: Surface: Python/JS library; the unit of behaviour is a compiled StateGraph (nodes = callables, edges, shared state, optional checkpointer/store) or LangChain create_agent's built-in model/tools loop with a middleware stack. Defaults: with no interrupt() call sites and no HITL middleware, nothing is gated — every proposed tool call executes in-process with host privileges; there is no default ask/deny and no no-match concept. Approval exists only where the owner built it (interrupt() sites, interrupt_on entries, custom wrap_tool_call/after_model hooks). Decision oracle: none — absent, not blocked. No Decision verdicts are issued; measurement proceeds via an evaluator-authored pinned reference agent at the Approval (interrupt stream) and Effect (sentinel/sandbox-diff instrument) layers.
